In the game of cricket, there are 11 batsmen who bat during the match of 50 overs. Two batsmen come to bat first and when any one of the two gets out, the next batsman comes to bat along with the one of the two batsmen left out, and so on — the next batsman comes to bat in a fixed sequence for all the three matches. Only one batsman can get out for one ball. One over comprises 6 balls, to be thrown one by one. If all the batsmen get out before the scheduled 50 overs, the match ends at that point (known as Overs Actually Played). The bar chart below shows total scheduled overs and overs actually played for the first match (denoted by 1), second match (denoted by 2) and third match (denoted by 3).

![overs chart](/di/mod/16-s2.png)

The table below shows the runs scored in the three-match series. Total runs scored = Runs scored by first five players + Runs scored by remaining last six players + Extra runs.

![runs table](/di/mod/16-s2b.png)
directions: Go through the data set given below and solve the questions based on it.
question_text: In which of the matches, Indian Team’s average runs per over is maximum?
explanation: Average runs per over = total runs / overs actually played. Match 1: 227/45 = 5.04; Match 2: 165/48 = 3.44; Match 3: 167/44 = 3.80. Maximum in the first match. Option (a).

directions: Go through the data set given below and solve the questions based on it.
question_text: What would have the total runs scored in the third match if Indian team would have played 50 overs with the same average which it maintained till the overs actually played?
explanation: Match 3 average = 167/44 ≈ 3.80 runs/over. Over a full 50 overs at the same average: 3.80 × 50 ≈ 190 runs. Option (b).

directions: Go through the data set given below and solve the questions based on it.
question_text: Mr Phani Ram, the team selector, has made following observations to improve the performance of the team: (i) Performance of first five players has improved, whereas performance of last six players has gone down. (ii) Had there been no extra runs, runs in second match would have decreased by maximum percentage. (iii) If team would have played for full 50 overs, it would have scored maximum in first match. How many of these observations are true?

options.label: a
options.text: Only I and II but not iii

options.label: b
options.text: Only ii and iii but not i

options.label: c
options.text: Only I and iii but not ii

explanation: (I) is true (first-five runs rose 18→80 while last-six fell 187→70). (II) is false — the maximum % drop with no extras is in Match 3 (~10.2%), not Match 2. (iii) is true — average runs/over is maximum in Match 1, so full-50-over runs would be maximum there. Only I and iii. Option (c).

directions: Go through the data set given below and solve the questions based on it.
question_text: If extra runs are not considered, which match has the lowest average runs per over?
explanation: Ignoring extras: Match 1 = 205/45 = 4.56; Match 2 = 147/48 = 3.06; Match 3 = 150/44 = 3.41. Lowest is the second match. Option (b).

context_passage:
The following bar chart represents the detail regarding the number of persons who attended the James Bond film festival named "Name is Bond", where four movies — The Man with the Golden Gun, Casino Royale, Goldfinger and Tomorrow Never Dies — were screened. Each person who attended the festival watched at least one of the four movies. Besides, there are four types of persons (of which the first three are characterized by age):
Type 1 — Age > 60 years, who watched the movie.
Type 2 — Age > 30 years but not more than 60 years, who watched the movie.
Type 3 — Age not more than 30 years, who watched the movie.
Type 4 — Persons who watched only that movie.

![film festival chart](/di/mod/16-s3.png)

All the data points are multiples of 10.
directions: Go through the data set given below and solve the questions based on it.
question_text: What could be the maximum number of persons who watched all the four movies?
explanation: The maximum who watched all four = sum of the minimum Type-1/2/3 counts across movies (30 + 50 + 60 = 140), but this is capped by each movie's 'only that movie' constraint. Goldfinger gives (40+50+60) − 140 = 10 vs 30 watching only it, forcing the maximum down to 120. Option (d).

directions: Go through the data set given below and solve the questions based on it.
question_text: What could be the maximum number of persons of age more than 60 years, who attended the festival?
explanation: The maximum number of persons older than 60 who attended is bounded by the Type-1 counts across the four movies under the overlap constraints, giving 140. Option (d).
